evidence:
Scope reviewed: 164 criteria (functional 152, polish 5, visual 5, two gates). The large majority meet the row well: each names an owned outcome, a positive control before any refusal/absence credit, a fresh or separate-context readback, and probes that separate near-miss implementations (e.g. functional/judge.toml:65 hro_money_precision uses 90071992547409.91 and 70368744177664.01, which are not exactly representable as doubles, so float parsing is caught; :434 hro_approval_budget separates run-rate from band basis and <= from <; :587 hro_months uses a one-millisecond boundary and Jan-31 clamping; :632 hro_competing re-reads persisted state after Promise.all; :1028 hro_change_aba distinguishes history from equal balance). Visual rows are likert with five described anchors on named surfaces, which the skill's known-false-positive list tells me to accept. I found no criterion that scores from source, and no pure 'looks right' binary.

Instances that do not meet the row (every one I found):

1. Stated property with no probe - functional/judge.toml:812, :821, :830 (hro_audit_text, hro_audit_revision, hro_audit_rescission): 'a human-readable immutable audit entry names its actor and target and summarizes before/after state'. Nothing in these rows, or in P4 (functional/prompt.md:39), re-reads the ordinary audit text line after a later action in the same lineage. hro_audit_readback (:839) only re-reads after a fresh sign-in ('This row judges fresh-sign-in persistence'); hro_afterimage_history (:875) covers structured snapshots only; hro_change_history (:1109) covers coordinated-change member text only. 'immutable' is therefore undecidable for ordinary approval/revision/rescission audit lines. Combined weight 0.3617 of 74.0 (0.49% of functional).

2. Status-only assertions, the skill's named defect 'a response-shape assertion with no state change':
   a. functional/judge.toml:758 hro_anon_read_status - 'Each must return401 ... This row owns the public unauthenticated response-status policy; each data family's confidentiality is scored independently'. By construction the row's only observable is an HTTP status on a read. 401 is a public rule (hireops_rules.md:370), so this is not a hidden requirement; it is a form defect. Weight 0.0689 (0.09%).
   b. functional/judge.toml:1190, :1208, :1226, :1244, :1262, :1280 hro_change_commit_<role>, second leg - 'Repeat against a committed operation to prove authorization precedes cached write results'. Replaying a commit of an already-committed operation changes no state whether the app returns 403 or the cached receipt, and every signed-in role may read receipts anyway (:1172 hro_change_readers), so the only distinguishing evidence is the status code. The first leg (eligible target, unchanged financial state) is properly outcome-based. Six rows, 0.36 total (0.49%).

3. Credit with no observation - functional/judge.toml:650 hro_draft_eligibility: 'If the optional history is omitted or no DRAFT is exposed, this condition is satisfied without requiring import.' An app that imports no history gets the row with nothing observed. This follows from instruction.md:17 (history optional), and weight is 0.01 (0.014%), so impact is negligible, but it is a criterion without an outcome on that branch.

4. Inconsistent tool name inside criterion/protocol text - the gates and most protocols name 'browser_run_code_unsafe' (functional/prompt.md:13, :19; judge.toml:632), while functional/judge.toml:1352 hro_live_committed_viewer says 'Read the Auditor's page inside browser_run_code in that context', and functional/prompt.md:77 and polish/prompt.md:16 also say 'browser_run_code'. tests/Dockerfile:19 pins @playwright/mcp@0.0.79; at most one of the two names exists there. I could not check which: no local install of that package, Docker not permitted for this assignment, and no configured judge transcript exists. hro_live_committed_viewer weighs 2.5 of 74.0 (3.4%).

Unmeasured, and the reason risk stays true independently of the instances above: raw-evidence-index.json states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and target/Oracle scores are absent. The golden has NOT been scripted through every Functional criterion'. So no run shows that the configured judge can actually perform the mechanisms many criteria depend on under playwright-mcp --headless --isolated: page.context().browser().newContext() (used by the in-dimension gate of all three scored prompts and by every clean-context/anonymous/L row), keeping a second context alive and readable across tool calls for the L rows and hro_pol_live_keeps_entries, page.route abort before dispatch (hro_keep_rescission_date :1388), and route.fetch() then route.abort() (polish hro_pol_uncertain_commit). The prompts do give an honest NOT EXERCISED path for tool limits, but that path scores 0, so an infeasible mechanism would be charged to the submission. Browser decidability of those rows is asserted, not demonstrated.

Not reported as instances: exact 403/409/401 plus unchanged-state rows (status is paired with a state readback and the codes are public at hireops_rules.md:370-371, :436, :453); the 15-second live rows (public at instruction.md:9, with a first-snapshot-at-or-after-15s tolerance at functional/prompt.md:77); the P5a 'no such claims satisfies' clauses (attached to rows that have their own owned observable); polish focus/scroll rows (document.activeElement and scrollY are readable, and the focus rule is public at hireops_rules.md:552-555).
counterexample: Broken app that passes: an app that renders each Audit Trail line from the current state of the offer rather than storing it, so an approval's line is rewritten (new before/after figures, or the target id swapped to the successor) once the offer is later revised. Immediately after the approval the line names actor and target and summarizes before/after, so hro_audit_text passes; hro_audit_readback passes because the line is still readable after a fresh Auditor sign-in if no later action intervened; hro_afterimage_history only checks structured snapshots. The stated 'immutable' bar is violated and no row observes it. Separately, for instance 2b: an app that answers a non-Finance commit replay of an already-committed operation with HTTP 200 and an empty body differs from a conforming app only in a status code, with no state or disclosure difference a browser user could see.
suggested_fix: Either delete 'immutable' from hro_audit_text/_revision/_rescission or give one row the probe (re-read the recorded ordinary audit line after a later action in the same lineage and require it unchanged); use one tool name consistently in hro_live_committed_viewer, functional/prompt.md:77 and polish/prompt.md:16 after confirming which name @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 exposes. Instances 2 and 3 are owner's call: fold the status policy into the confidentiality/state rows or record them as accepted status-only rows. Before clearance, obtain one configured-judge transcript showing newContext, cross-call second-context reads and both route interceptions work.
